posts.title: Friday Roundtable: Holiday Buses and Trains
posts.description: MEHVA and the Mt. Rainier Scenic Railroad have seasonal trips to celebrate the holidays on historic transit vehicles. (MEHVA and Mt. Rainier Scenic Railroad) The holiday season is upon us and there are few better ways to celebrate than on board a historic transit vehicle. This year, the Metro Employees Historic Vehicle Association’s (MEHVA) Holiday Lights Tour is on December 5. Climb aboard a preserved Metro bus and enjoy a trip through several Seattle neighborhoods to see the best holiday lights in the City. The 2 hour tour starts at 7pm, one block east of Stadium station. Tickets and more information can be found on MEHVA’s website . Between now and December 23, Mt. Rainier Scenic Railroad is running the Steam Into Christmas experience. The 75-minute journey/show takes place on vintage passenger cars pulled by either the 104-year-old Polson Logging No. 70 or the 102-year-old Porter No. 5 locomotive. Trips run every Thursday, Friday, Saturday, and Sunday, as well as on December 21-23.

posts.title: Elevated line to Ballard
posts.description: At the Ballard Town Hall meeting somebody asked whether Sound Transit had considered elevating the line instead of tunneling to reduce cost and build it earlier. Sound Transit’s response was that they cannot imagine any way to build an elevated Link light rail line through downtown and meet current environmental requirements. An elevated line would certainly be cheaper and faster to build and easier for riders to access than the currently planned deep tunnel. Could any of the alternative modes I described make it possible to build an elevated line through downtown? Modern guideway design ( Grab Lab ) As Kubly/Reed recently pointed out, current Link trains needs very long stations. That makes it difficult to find a location for an underground station which does not interfere with existing building foundations, but also to fit an elevated station into the existing street valleys. posts.title: Sound Transit Debuts Refurbished Kinkisharyo Link Trains
posts.description: LRV 110 on the 2 Line at Pioneer Square station. The external facing displays on the retrofitted trains show the route number, color, and last stop. This morning, Sound Transit quietly launched the first refurbished Kinkisharyo trainset on the 2 Line. After years of design and months of testing, light-rail vehicles 110 and 113 ran a roundtrip between Redmond and Lynnwood during the morning rush hour. Part of the initial Link fleet delivered in 2006, these vehicles have been out of service for a deep refurbishment that saw upgrades to the train’s electrical and communication systems. In 2022, Sound Transit contracted Woojin IS America to refresh the 62 Kinkisharyo trains, also knows as Series 1. These trains were delivered between 2006 and 2011 and include some now-outdated components. Replacing these will allow the vehicles to remain in a state of good repair for the next 15 years.
